<CoreConceptHeader
  title="Sizing"
  description="The sizing system provides a consistent way to define and manage element dimensions."
  image="core_sizing_docs.svg"
/>

  The sizing system in Ignite UI Theming provides a consistent way to define and manage element dimensions. Instead of hardcoding fixed values, you can define up to three distinct size states — `small`, `medium`, and `large`, and switch between them dynamically.

  Key benefits of using the sizing system are:

  - Making it easy to switch between sizes globally or per component.
  - Reduces hardcoded values, improving maintainability.
  - Keeps your styles flexible and ready for growth.

  To make an element dynamically sizable, you would need to: 

  - First, include the `sizable{:sass}` mixin in the element’s styles. This sets up the necessary CSS variables and structure for the sizing system to work.

  ```scss
  .wrapper {
    // Make the element sizable
    @include sizable();
  }
  ```

	- Then, you can define the sizes for the element using the `sizable(){:js}` function. It accepts three parameters for the small, medium, and large sizes. The function will declare CSS variables for each size based on the passed values.

	```scss
	.wrapper {
      // Define sizes for small (60%), medium (80%), and large (100%)
      width: sizable($sm: 60%, $md: 80%, $lg: 100%);
	}
	```

	- Finally to set the element to a specific size, you just need to assign the corresponding CSS variable to the `--component-size{:sass}` variable. Here the element will be set to medium size by assigning `var(--ig-size-medium){:sass}` to `--component-size{:sass}`. 

  ```scss
  .wrapper {
    // Sets the element to use the medium size - (--ig-size-medium)
    --component-size: var(--ig-size-medium);
  }
  ```

	You can easily switch it to small or large by changing the assigned variable to `var(--ig-size-small){:sass}` or `var(--ig-size-large){:sass}`, respectively.

	<SizesSample />
  <br/>
  Here, the `.wrapper{:css}` element has assigned three different sizes: `60%{:sass}`, `80%{:sass}`, and `100%{:sass}`, for its width property. These can be easily changed through the value of the `--component-size{:sass}` variable, making the element’s width easily switchable.
